summary: Modern databases and data platforms have increasingly embedded AI/ML capabilities directly into their engines, ranging from in-database model training (SQL-based ML) to native vector search and managed LLM access for retrieval-augmented generation. Industry analysts project rapid adoption of vector-based retrieval, with Gartner forecasting 30% of enterprises relying on vector retrieval for GenAI by 2026 and the vector database market expected to reach ~USD 17.91 billion by 2034. The result is a convergence where operational databases, analytical warehouses, and lakehouses all offer some combination of embeddings generation, vector similarity search, and LLM integration without requiring separate AI infrastructure.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, embeddings) plus Snowflake Postgres with Cortex access
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs and embedding models directly via SQL and Python, enabling text completion, summarization, translation, sentiment analysis, and RAG. Cortex Search offers a managed hybrid (vector + keyword) retrieval service. Snowflake Postgres extends these capabilities to Postgres applications while keeping data in-platform.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with built-in vector similarity functions and the managed Cortex Search service for semantic/hybrid retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Native managed LLMs via Cortex (e.g., Snowflake Arctic, and third-party models such as Llama, Mistral, Claude) accessible through SQL/Python functions without managing AI infrastructure.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex functions billed per token/credit usage on top of standard Snowflake compute and storage credits.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (in-database model training via SQL) integrated with Vertex AI foundation models
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, etc.) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call Gemini and other foundation models for generative tasks, embeddings generation, and remote model inference directly from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides VECTOR_SEARCH functions and vector indexes for approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI / Gemini via remote models and ML.GENERATE_TEXT / ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions callable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-as-you-go based on bytes processed (queries) and slot/compute usage; Vertex AI model calls and embeddings incur separate Vertex AI charges.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database LLM and embedding workflows
databases.description: PostgreSQL itself has no built-in AI, but the open-source pgvector extension adds a vector data type with similarity search (HNSW and IVFFlat indexes), and pgai (from Timescale) adds SQL functions to generate embeddings and call LLM providers. Together they turn Postgres into a capable RAG and semantic search backend.
databases.vector_search_notes: Via extension (pgvector), not core. Self-managed/community PostgreSQL requires installing pgvector; it is not part of the base engine, though it is widely bundled by managed providers.
databases.llm_integration: Through pgai and related extensions that call external LLM/embedding APIs (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) from SQL; no native hosted models in core Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; costs depend on hosting/compute and any third-party LLM API usage for embeddings and completions.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-based invocation of Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend models
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you call external AWS ML services directly from SQL queries, passing database rows to SageMaker-hosted models, Amazon Comprehend (sentiment/NLP), or Amazon Bedrock foundation models for inference and generating embeddings, then returning results inline.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is provided via the pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML integration feature.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock (foundation models/LLMs) and SageMaker from SQL; combined with pgvector this enables RAG, but LLM access is via external AWS services.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora compute/storage/I-O pricing plus separately billed SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend inference costs for each model invocation.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — create and run ML models via SQL using Amazon SageMaker (Autopilot) and Bedrock
databases.description: Redshift ML enables analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, with SageMaker Autopilot handling model selection in the background. It also supports bring-your-own-model and integration with Bedrock LLMs for generative tasks on warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively built into Redshift ML as a general-purpose vector search engine; Redshift has limited/emerging vector support but vector similarity search is not its primary native capability. For production vector workloads AWS typically points to OpenSearch, Aurora/pgvector, or dedicated vector stores.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock models invoked from SQL for predictions and generative AI on warehouse data.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed on Redshift compute/storage; model training/inference via SageMaker and Bedrock incurs separate charges based on usage.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) with Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks offers an end-to-end AI stack on the lakehouse: Mosaic AI for model fine-tuning, serving, foundation model APIs, and agent frameworks, plus a managed Vector Search service that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a fully managed, built-in service that creates and maintains vector indexes synced with Delta tables.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to open and proprietary LLMs (e.g., Llama, DBRX, and external models) for inference, fine-tuning, and agent workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute and model serving; Vector Search and foundation model APIs billed separately based on usage/throughput.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search — native vector indexing and search in MongoDB's document model
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational documents and run approximate nearest neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, enabling semantic search and RAG directly in MongoDB Atlas with hybrid search combining vector and metadata filters.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is a built-in Atlas feature using dedicated vector indexes and the $vectorSearch operator; no external extension required.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs of its own, but integrates with external model providers (OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex, etc.) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex to generate embeddings and power RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Part of MongoDB Atlas; billed on cluster/compute tier with vector search indexes consuming additional memory/storage; dedicated Search Nodes can be provisioned at extra cost.
